This new awareness of society as a fact of human existence led Locke to acknowledge that individuality could only exist in relation to others and to the community at large. He therefore concluded that man has a duty to respect the rights of his fellow men, and that he cannot claim unlimited liberty of action if it infringes on the same right of others.
